 F10.02: FactoryTalk View SE Security 
 Use a password-protected screen saver.  To ensure that only operators with the proper 
credentials are accessing workstations in a closed system, a password-protected screen 
saver can be used on the FactoryTalk View SE Client terminals.  This system will take the recommended exception to this rule when critical process data must be displayed at all times.  In this case, a ‘view only’ user account will be logged in to display the status of production and alarm information.  
 Use the included DeskLock software feature to restrict operators’ access to the client’s 
operating system.  
 Disable switch to other applications since this opens access to other programs.  
 Disable ‘Allow display code debugging’  since this allows launching of the VBA editor, 
which is not secure. 
 Change the window properties of the FactoryTalk View SE Client to disable the title 
bar, the system menu, the close button, and the show diagnostics list.  Set the window to be maximized. 
 F10.03: Configure FactoryTalk View SE clients automatically login as DEFAULT user 
after a period of inactivity 
Since the system requires that critical operations  information be displayed at all times, the DEFAULT 
User (a user with ‘view only’ access) shall be logged in when a period of inactivity occurs.  This allows the read-only display of production and alarm information.  
FactoryTalk View SE clients can be configured to automatically log out after a specified 
period of time, however this feature does not subsequently permit the immediate and automatic login of another user (DEFAULT) as required.  To achieve the required actions, idle conditions will be detected and then the DEFAULT user will be logged in effectively logging out the current user.

F09.00: Physical Security 
It is essential to limit operator access to  the hardware running Windows operating systems and 
FactoryTalk View SE.  In general, an operator’s only access to the computer should be via the keyboard, mouse, or touch screen.  An operator with access to the power switch and bootable media 
could have direct access to the underlying file syst em and could potentially circumvent many of the 
security measures described in this document.  It is the responsibility of the Mark Cuban Cost Plus 
Drug Company, PBC. to put measures in place to limit operator access and to protect the hardware systems.

 F10.01: System Security Configuration 
Security is used to restrict a user’s access to certain parts of the system.  FactoryTalk View SE uses a 
combination of Microsoft Windows domain security and FactoryTalk View SE security.  While Windows security is used to authenticate users and restrict operating system level actions, FactoryTalk View SE runtime security restricts graphical user interface access and control system function access.  The 
FactoryTalk View SE security is based on a system of letter codes (A-P) which are assigned to the 
individual users to define their access.

UR5.2.5 [URS-PCS-SR-011] System must be capable of utilizing active directory. It must be possible to 
configure the required password strength of the user’s password  with items such as # of 
capital letters, # of special characters,  and length of the password itself.     
 
Both Microsoft Windows domain security and the FactoryTalk System Administration tool can enable the 
creation of a unique login and password for each user. 
FactoryTalk View SE can use Microsoft Windows security to manage user accounts. Password 
expiration, password aging, password complexity  requirements, account expiration, disabling of 
accounts, lockout aftern invalid login attempts, and forcing a change of password on first login are all security features provided by both Microso ft Windows security and FactoryTalk Security. 
Procedures should be implemented to ensure that user IDs do not get deleted or reassigned.  It is 
recommended to disable user IDs rather than deleting them as a best practice. 
The customer’s management procedure should include the verification of the identity of an individual 
before sanctioning an individual’s electronic signature. 
Once a user has been sanctioned and a unique account with password has been created in the 
FactoryTalk View SE system, the user is required to enter his/ her login and password to access FactoryTalk View SE. This process validates the identity of the user to FactoryTalk View SE. 
FactoryTalk View SE requires two components for us er identification: a unique login ID and password. 
When using the FactoryTalk View SE electronic signature feature, both the user login ID and password 
are required to perform an action.  The FactoryTalk View SE electronic signature feature can be configured to display and record the meaning of the signature. It also allows for separate performer and approval signatures, and for comments to be added regarding the meaning of the signature. 
If the user logs out of FactoryTalk View SE and again requires access, the user must reenter the login ID 
and password.

 F05.01: Trending 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.2.19 [URS-PCS-SR-025] Real-time multi-pen trends  for all analog and defined discrete signals.  Also, 
PID loop controller screens to include trending for PV, SP and CV as applicable.  
 
The system provides the ability to trend any of the tags in the PCS-CP01 PLC controller which 
includes both analog and discrete signals.  Tags can be added and removed at runtime.  The 
trending requirement for the PV, SP, and CV of the PID loops does not apply since there are no PID 
loops under the control of the PCS-CP01 system.   
 F05.02: Display colors of dynamic objects 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.2.20 [URS-PCS-SR-026] The following colors shall be utilized when indicat ing states of dynamic 
objects…(see below)  
 
The following colors shall be utilized when indicating states of dynamic objects:  1. Gray – General meaning is “Not Operating” (e.g., motor not running, device is de-
energized, valve is closed).  
2. Green – General meaning is “Operating” (e.g., motor is running, device is energized, 
valve is open.). 
3. Yellow – General meaning is “Warning” or “Take Note” (e.g., device is in a mode 
other than normal such as manual mode, valve is in an intermediate state such as 
manual mode, valve is in an intermediate state such as traveling between closed and open).  
4. Red – General meaning is “Alarm” or “Lockout” (e.g., an alarm is active on a device or 
Operation, lockout is activated).  
The color palette is applied to dynamic objects to reflect the colors shown above.
